newsitem.title: USA: IMF official optimistic on resumed loan to Russia.
newsitem.headline: IMF official optimistic on resumed loan to Russia.

text.p: A senior International Monetary Fund official voiced optimism on Monday that the agency will approve Russia's 1997 economic plan and resume lending to Moscow soon, possibly in the next month.
"We are extemely positive of what could be done during the next month," said the official, who declined to be named.
The IMF has delayed payments to Russia for a few months under a $10 billion loan deal largely because of concerns about its low tax revenues.

Speaking to reporters ahead of this week's semi-annual meeting of the IMF and World Bank, the Fund official said that Russia was headed by an "extremely determined" team that knows what needs to be done to put the economy on track.
"I think they will do that," he added.
The new Russian team, the result of a cabinet reshuffle last month, is headed by leading economic reformer and one-time privatization chief Anatoly Chubais.
An IMF mission arrived in Moscow on Monday to finalize work on Russia's economic program for 1997.
Agreement on the 1997 program would open the door for resumed IMF lending to Moscow.
Chubais has been quoted as saying that this year's loan payments could be the last time that Russia turns to the IMF for funds.
The IMF official welcomed that because it would mean that Russia had proceeded well along the path of turning its economy from communism to capitalism.
